text:
Elias Lindholm scored four goals against Washington on Saturday, the first four-goal game of his career, and that night sums up his season: real chances, and a lot of them going in. He has 11 goals and 22 points in 23 games, and our wins-added measure has him ninth of 560 skaters, with his goals swinging more games than chance quality alone would explain.

The process is better than it was. With him on the ice at five on five, Boston has taken 59% of the expected goals, the share of quality chances, 7.6 points better than without him, and his own chances over the last ten games ran above his usual rate. That's a turnaround from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him at replacement level.

The finishing is the part to be careful with. He's shooting 24% against 15% last season, and the Bruins have scored 5.8 more goals than expected with him out there. Our range puts his true shooting between 13% and 18%. Watch the deflections and royal-road looks (Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 23% of his setups crossing the slot last season); the chances should stay even if the percentage drifts back.
